Level two. You got into Berkeley. But your iron lung won't fit in a dorm room. Where do you live?
This was a real level. California, nineteen sixty-two.
Ed Roberts got polio at fourteen. It paralyzed him from the neck down, and he slept in an iron lung.
The state called him too disabled to hold a job. And Berkeley said its dorms couldn't take him.
So, pick your fix. A: study from home. B: wait for a bigger dorm. C: move into the campus hospital.
A fails. You can't get to class from your bedroom.
B fails. Nobody was building one.
C worked. Ed moved into an empty hospital wing. More disabled students followed, and called themselves the Rolling Quads.
In nineteen seventy-six, the state agency that said he couldn't hold a job made him its director.
Today, the A.D.A. says a curb ramp can rise one inch for every twelve, at most.
Level cleared. Comment what you picked, and follow for level three.
